definition: The central application object that implements a WSGI application and acts as a registry for view functions, URL rules, template configuration, and more.
A way to organize a group of related views and other code. Blueprints are registered on the application and help structure larger applications into modular components.
An environment created for each request that makes flask.request point to the current request object.
An environment that makes flask.current_app point to the active application. Used to access application-level resources outside of request handling.
Web Server Gateway Interface — a standard Python interface for web applications. Flask's wsgi_app() method is the actual WSGI application.
The name of a URL rule, usually the same name as the view function. Used internally for URL building and routing.
A Python function that handles requests to a specific URL and returns a response. Decorated with @app.route().
A string pattern that maps URLs to view functions. Registered using route() decorator or add_url_rule() method.
The absolute path to the package on the filesystem. Used to look up resources contained in the package.
An alternative folder for instance-specific configuration and data files. By default a folder named 'instance' next to the package.
The folder containing static files (CSS, JavaScript, images) served by the application. Defaults to 'static'.
The folder containing Jinja2 templates used for rendering responses. Defaults to 'templates'.
A dictionary-like object (Flask.config) that stores configuration variables used by the application and extensions.
Functions decorated with @app.before_request() that execute before each request is dispatched.
Functions decorated with @app.after_request() that execute after the response is generated, before sending.
Functions that execute after a request is complete, even if an exception occurred. Used for cleanup like closing database connections.
Functions decorated with @app.context_processor() that return dictionaries of variables added to every template's context.
Custom functions registered with @app.template_filter() usable in Jinja2 templates to transform values.
Functions registered with @app.errorhandler() that handle specific HTTP status codes or exception types.
Created by test_client(), allows making requests to the application without running a live server. Used for unit testing.
Server-side or cookie-based storage of data across requests for a particular user.
The template engine used by Flask for rendering HTML templates with dynamic content.
In Flask, a Python decorator that registers functions for specific purposes (routing, error handling, request hooks).
The object returned by a view function containing the data sent back to the client.
The object containing all data about the incoming HTTP request (headers, form data, args, files).
Software that wraps the WSGI application to modify requests or responses before/after the application processes them.
A configuration flag enabling automatic code reloading and interactive debugging.
Created by create_url_adapter(), matches incoming requests to URL rules and provides URL building capabilities.
The default session interface that stores session data in encrypted cookies on the client side.
